mechanism: This paper tests MEKi (selumetinib) as monotherapy and combined with FTY720: it reduces neurofibroma number in DhhCre;Nf1fl/fl mice, inhibits tumor sphere formation from mouse/human Schwann cell progenitors, suppresses Schwann cell growth/migration, and increases apoptosis.
annotation_note: MEK1/2 has approved inhibitors (selumetinib) with direct pharmacology on RAS-pathway-driven Schwann-lineage tumor cells, relevant to essentially all NF1-driven tumors.

mechanism: Selumetinib, an oral MEK1/2 inhibitor blocking RAS/MAPK pathway overactive due to neurofibromin loss, produced durable plexiform neurofibroma shrinkage and clinically meaningful decreases in tumor-related pain intensity and interference.
annotation_note: MEK1/2 has approved inhibitors (selumetinib) with direct pharmacology on RAS-pathway-driven Schwann-lineage tumor cells, relevant to essentially all NF1-driven tumors.

mechanism: PRC2 complex (EED/SUZ12) is biallelically inactivated via somatic SVs in a subset of MPNSTs, causing H3K27me3 loss, distinct genomic evolution (near-haploidization, WGD, chr8 amplification), reduced immune infiltration, and worse prognosis in NF1 patients.
mutation_context: Biallelic somatic SV-mediated inactivation of EED/SUZ12 (PRC2 loss), found in a subset (~50-80%) of MPNSTs, not all NF1 tumors
annotation_note: PRC2 loss is a tumor-suppressor lesion (nothing to inhibit) best used as a prognostic/stratification biomarker, acting tumor-cell-intrinsically in a genomically-defined MPNST subset.

mechanism: NF1-associated OPGs arise from biallelic NF1-inactivated glioma stem cells/astrocytes with haploinsufficient stromal microenvironment; MEK inhibition (selumetinib) targets Ras/MAPK dysregulation, showing activity in NF1-associated LGG trials.
annotation_note: MEK1/2 has approved inhibitors (selumetinib) with direct pharmacology on RAS-pathway-driven Schwann-lineage tumor cells, relevant to essentially all NF1-driven tumors.

mechanism: NF1-associated OPGs arise from biallelic NF1-inactivated glioma stem cells/astrocytes with haploinsufficient stromal microenvironment; MEK inhibition (selumetinib) targets Ras/MAPK dysregulation, showing activity in NF1-associated LGG trials.
annotation_note: MEK1/2 has approved inhibitors (selumetinib) with direct pharmacology on RAS-pathway-driven Schwann-lineage tumor cells, relevant to essentially all NF1-driven tumors.

mechanism: Merlin/NF2 loss activates mTORC1 (pS6) and mTORC2 (pAkt, SGK1, pNDRG1) in VS cells; combined AZD2014 (mTORC1/2 inhibitor) and dasatinib synergistically reduce metabolic activity and inhibit tumor growth in vitro and in vivo.
annotation_note: mTOR is directly druggable (everolimus, AZD2014) acting on the tumor cell itself in NF1/NF2-driven tumors, relevant across essentially all patients with these manifestations.

mechanism: Cav2.2 (CACNA1B) currents/CGRP release increased in Nf1+/- sensory neurons via CRMP2 interaction; t-CNRP1 disrupts CRMP2-Cav2.2 binding, reducing Ca2+ influx and pain behaviors
annotation_note: Cav2.2 is a druggable ion channel (ziconotide precedent) driving CGRP release from sensory neurons, relevant to all Nf1+/- pain, not tumor/stroma.

mechanism: Bevacizumab (anti-VEGF antibody) given to NF2 vestibular schwannoma patients; systematic review found 41% tumor regression, 20% hearing improvement, 69% no further hearing loss; dose-dependent toxicity noted.
annotation_note: VEGFA is directly druggable (bevacizumab shows clinical efficacy in NF2 schwannoma) and acts via anti-angiogenic effects on tumor endothelium, not the Schwann-lineage tumor cell.

mechanism: Trametinib (MEK1/2i) monotherapy causes only transient ERK suppression, feedback RTK/RAS-GTP upregulation, and minimal antitumor effect in NF1-MPNST allografts/PDX; inferior to SHP2 inhibition, not to CDK4/6i combination as claimed.
annotation_note: MEK1/2 has approved inhibitors (selumetinib) with direct pharmacology on RAS-pathway-driven Schwann-lineage tumor cells, relevant to essentially all NF1-driven tumors.

mechanism: Consensus paper lists TP53 inactivating mutation as a sufficient molecular feature for MPNST diagnosis in NF1; TP53-altered MPNST show worse outcomes.
mutation_context: TP53 inactivating mutation/deletion in TP53-altered MPNST, a subset of NF1-associated MPNST (not present in benign neurofibromas or germline NF1 loss)
annotation_note: TP53 loss is undruggable directly and serves as a diagnostic/prognostic marker restricted to the TP53-altered MPNST subset, acting tumor-cell-intrinsically.

mechanism: mTORC1/mTORC2 activated in NF2-deficient meningioma cells; dual mTORC1/2 inhibitor combined with dasatinib produced strong growth inhibition in orthotopic model.
annotation_note: mTOR is directly druggable (everolimus, AZD2014) acting on the tumor cell itself in NF1/NF2-driven tumors, relevant across essentially all patients with these manifestations.

mechanism: PI3K inhibition (pictilisib) reduces viability/growth of merlin-deficient Schwann cells in vitro and, combined with PAK inhibitor PF-3758309, reduces orthotopic schwannoma allograft growth via decreased proliferation and increased apoptosis.
annotation_note: PI3K inhibitors (e.g., pictilisib) directly target hyperactivated PI3K in tumour Schwann/glioma cells downstream of NF1/NF2 loss, present in essentially all patients.

mechanism: AURKA overexpressed in MPNST vs neurofibromas; AURKA siRNA and small-molecule inhibitors (e.g., MLN8237) preferentially reduced viability of NF1-mutant MPNST cell lines over NF2 lines.
annotation_note: AURKA is a druggable kinase (MLN8237/alisertib is clinical-stage) acting directly on NF1-mutant MPNST tumor cells, not a mutation-restricted biomarker or stromal target.

mechanism: Serum AXL was significantly lower in NF1 patients with MPNST than those with high-load plexiform neurofibromas; AXL levels correlated with internal tumor burden, not significantly different from no-tumor patients.
annotation_note: Used here as a serum biomarker tracking tumor burden, not a drug target; AXL itself is druggable (e.g. bemcentinib) but acts mainly via TME/endothelial-immune signaling.

mechanism: Serum PD-L1 (CD274) significantly elevated in NF1 patients with MPNST versus those with plexiform neurofibroma or no tumor; authors propose it as biomarker and rationale for anti-PD-L1/PD-1 checkpoint immunotherapy.
annotation_note: Approved anti-PD-L1/PD-1 checkpoint agents exist, but here CD274 is used as a serum stratification biomarker and would act on tumor-infiltrating T cells/immune microenvironment, not the Schwann-lineage tumor cell.

mechanism: CRMP2 binds neurofibromin and Cav2.2; loss of neurofibromin frees CRMP2 to bind syntaxin1A/Cav2.2, increasing CGRP release; t-CNRP1 peptide reverses inflammatory, postsurgical, neuropathic pain
annotation_note: CRMP2 is druggable directly (t-CNRP1 peptide disrupts CRMP2-Cav2.2 to block CGRP release); relevant to all NF1 patients via germline neurofibromin loss, acting on sensory neurons, not TME.

mechanism: PAK inhibitor PF-3758309 combined with PI3K inhibitor pictilisib synergistically reduced merlin-deficient Schwann cell viability, decreased proliferation (Ki67), increased apoptosis, and reduced orthotopic vestibular schwannoma allograft tumor growth in mice.
annotation_note: PAK has clinical-stage inhibitors (PF-3758309) acting directly on merlin-deficient Schwann tumor cells, relevant to all NF2-SWN patients, not a specific subgenotype.

mechanism: This review states RASopathies, including NF1, are caused by germline mutations in components/regulators of the RAS/MAPK pathway (neurofibromin as RAS-GAP).
annotation_note: RAS itself is now directly druggable (KRAS G12C/G12D inhibitors, pan-RAS/SOS1 agents) and acts on tumor Schwann-lineage cells via MAPK hyperactivation, relevant across NF1/SWN broadly, not a restricted subgroup.

mechanism: LZTR1 mutations dysregulate RAS ubiquitination, causing impaired degradation of RAS superfamily proteins; loss-of-function LZTR1 variants remove negative regulation of RAS/MAPK signaling, driving proliferation and schwannoma development.
annotation_note: RAS itself is now directly druggable (KRAS G12C/G12D inhibitors, pan-RAS/SOS1 agents) and acts on tumor Schwann-lineage cells via MAPK hyperactivation, relevant across NF1/SWN broadly, not a restricted subgroup.

mechanism: CUDC907 (fimepinostat), a dual HDAC/PI3K inhibitor, lowered YAP levels and reduced viability/growth in schwannoma xenograft models and primary vestibular schwannoma cells.
annotation_note: YAP acts downstream of merlin loss in tumour cells itself; druggable indirectly via CUDC907, which lowers YAP and reduces schwannoma/meningioma cell viability.

mechanism: Loss of the CDKN2A/9p21 locus encoding p16 characterizes one of the earliest steps in malignant transformation of neurofibromas to MPNST.
mutation_context: CDKN2A/9p21 (p16) homozygous deletion, found in a subset of atypical neurofibromas and most MPNSTs, not present in benign plexiform neurofibromas
annotation_note: CDKN2A loss is a tumor-suppressor deletion best used as a diagnostic/prognostic marker of malignant progression, not a druggable target, and acts within the Schwann-cell lineage.

mechanism: Cdkn2a loss combined with Nf1 loss abrogates senescence checkpoint in Schwann cells, enabling progression from neurofibroma to atypical neurofibroma (GEM-ANF) and subsequent transformation to MPNST-like tumors.
mutation_context: CDKN2A/9p21 (p16) homozygous deletion, found in a subset of atypical neurofibromas and most MPNSTs, not present in benign plexiform neurofibromas
annotation_note: CDKN2A loss is a tumor-suppressor deletion best used as a diagnostic/prognostic marker of malignant progression, not a druggable target, and acts within the Schwann-cell lineage.

mechanism: Neurofibromin is a RAS/MAPK negative regulator; NF1 loss in Hoxb7-lineage Schwann cell precursors drives cutaneous and plexiform neurofibroma formation, with Hippo pathway dysregulation enhancing MAPK/p-ERK activation from NF1 loss.
annotation_note: RAS itself is now directly druggable (KRAS G12C/G12D inhibitors, pan-RAS/SOS1 agents) and acts on tumor Schwann-lineage cells via MAPK hyperactivation, relevant across NF1/SWN broadly, not a restricted subgroup.

mechanism: NF1 mutated in 15% of GBM; mTOR pathway constitutively active in NF1-deficient cells; rapamycin sensitivity shown mainly in MPNST and low-grade optic glioma models.
annotation_note: mTOR is directly druggable (everolimus, AZD2014) acting on the tumor cell itself in NF1/NF2-driven tumors, relevant across essentially all patients with these manifestations.

mechanism: SUZ12 inactivating mutation (PRC2 subunit) proposed as sufficient molecular feature for MPNST diagnosis, correlating with H3K27me3 loss in most MPNST.
mutation_context: SUZ12 (or EED) inactivating mutation causing PRC2 loss-of-function, found in ~70-90% of high-grade/malignant MPNST but not other NF1 manifestations
annotation_note: SUZ12 loss (PRC2 inactivation, H3K27me3 loss) is a diagnostic/subtyping marker for MPNST, not a direct drug target; no inhibitor restores a tumour-suppressor deletion.

mechanism: mTOR is a key downstream signaling node regulating cell growth/proliferation; everolimus (mTOR inhibitor) tested in phase II trials for recurrent/progressive pediatric LGG including NF1-associated OPG, showing partial responses.
annotation_note: mTOR is directly druggable (everolimus, AZD2014) acting on the tumor cell itself in NF1/NF2-driven tumors, relevant across essentially all patients with these manifestations.

mechanism: PRC2 (SUZ12) loss in 2KO cells disrupts pluripotency, induces MSC-like features, causes chromatin reorganization and neuro-mesenchymal transcriptional programs mimicking PNF-ANNUBP-MPNST progression.
mutation_context: Biallelic somatic SV-mediated inactivation of EED/SUZ12 (PRC2 loss), found in a subset (~50-80%) of MPNSTs, not all NF1 tumors
annotation_note: PRC2 loss is a tumor-suppressor lesion (nothing to inhibit) best used as a prognostic/stratification biomarker, acting tumor-cell-intrinsically in a genomically-defined MPNST subset.

mechanism: Selumetinib significantly improved VCI, PSI, and FSIQ scores in children and adults after 12-26 cycles; borderline/overt intellectual disability proportions decreased; improvement speculatively attributed to restored RAS-MAPK activity.
annotation_note: MEK1/2 has approved inhibitors (selumetinib) with direct pharmacology on RAS-pathway-driven Schwann-lineage tumor cells, relevant to essentially all NF1-driven tumors.

mechanism: NF1 loss hyperactivates RAS/MEK and PI3K-mTOR effector pathways driving MPNST; trial tested combined MEK (selumetinib) and mTOR (sirolimus) inhibition as therapeutic strategy.
annotation_note: mTOR is directly druggable (everolimus, AZD2014) acting on the tumor cell itself in NF1/NF2-driven tumors, relevant across essentially all patients with these manifestations.

mechanism: NF1 loss in Hoxb7-lineage Schwann cell precursors causes biallelic Nf1 inactivation, driving MAPK/RAS pathway hyperactivation (increased p-ERK1/2) and generating diffuse cutaneous neurofibroma, modifiable by Hippo pathway alterations.
annotation_note: RAS itself is now directly druggable (KRAS G12C/G12D inhibitors, pan-RAS/SOS1 agents) and acts on tumor Schwann-lineage cells via MAPK hyperactivation, relevant across NF1/SWN broadly, not a restricted subgroup.

mechanism: Neurofibromin loss causes RAS hyperactivation increasing GABAergic transmission, impairing LTP and causing social/spatial learning deficits in Nf1+/- mice; KRAS/NRAS depletion or MEK/RAS normalization reverses deficits.
annotation_note: RAS itself is now directly druggable (KRAS G12C/G12D inhibitors, pan-RAS/SOS1 agents) and acts on tumor Schwann-lineage cells via MAPK hyperactivation, relevant across NF1/SWN broadly, not a restricted subgroup.

mechanism: BIRC5/Survivin upregulated in NF1-mutant MPNST; pharmacologic (YM155, LQZ-7I) and siRNA inhibition selectively reduced viability of MPNST cells and Nf1-null Schwann precursors.
annotation_note: Survivin is directly druggable (YM155, LQZ-7I) in NF1-null Schwann-lineage tumor cells themselves, not a stratifying marker or microenvironment target.

mechanism: IMC shows CD44+ Schwann cells significantly more abundant in bevacizumab-treated (failure) VS versus treatment-naive, enriched in CN Bev-9, suggesting ECM remodeling/fibrosis linked to bevacizumab resistance.
annotation_note: CD44 marks fibrotic/ECM-remodeled Schwann cells linked to bevacizumab resistance and macrophage-SCP crosstalk, favoring biomarker/stromal-signaling use over direct tumor-cell drug target.

mechanism: Lapatinib (EGFR/ErbB2 inhibitor) inhibited VS growth in vitro; phase II trial in 21 NF2 patients showed ≥15% tumor volume reduction in 23.5% and hearing improvement in 30.8%, low toxicity.
annotation_note: EGFR is druggable on the tumor cell itself (lapatinib clinically active in NF2 VS/meningioma); relevant broadly via NF2-loss-driven EGFR upregulation, not a specific subset mutation.

mechanism: EphA2, previously shown upregulated/activated in NF2-deficient cells, was inhibited by brigatinib in Ben-Men-1 meningioma cells with ligand stimulation, reducing downstream AKT/ERK signaling.
annotation_note: EphA2 is directly druggable (brigatinib inhibition reduces AKT/ERK) in NF2-deficient meningioma tumor cells; relevant to all NF2-SWN patients, not a stromal target.

mechanism: GDNF mRNA/protein is selectively upregulated in Schwann cells/satellite glia of Nf1-mutant mice independent of tumors; GDNF-targeting antibody treatment rescues mechanical hypersensitivity, supporting SC-derived GDNF as a pain driver.
annotation_note: GDNF-neutralizing antibody is a credible pharmacological approach targeting Schwann/satellite glia-secreted ligand driving pain, a stromal/nerve microenvironment mechanism relevant to all Nf1-deficient patients.

mechanism: FT895, an HDAC11 inhibitor (IC50 3nM), disrupts mitochondrial biogenesis/function in MPNST cells, increasing ROS, decreasing mtDNA copy number, impairing respiration; enhances cordycepin cytotoxicity.
annotation_note: HDAC11 has a potent selective inhibitor (FT895) acting directly on MPNST tumor cells via mitochondrial disruption, relevant across NF1 patients, not a specific genotype subset.

mechanism: APEX-MS shows selumetinib increases KRAS (not NRAS/HRAS) proximity to neurofibromin; pan-KRAS inhibitor BI-2865 suppresses pERK, CDK1/2, ERK1/2; CRISPRi KRAS repression, not NRAS/HRAS, sensitizes to selumetinib.
annotation_note: KRAS is directly druggable (pan-KRAS BI-2865) and mediates MAPK signaling in NF1-null Schwann cell tumors, not genotype-restricted since NF1 loss is universal in plexiform neurofibroma.

mechanism: MEK inhibitor selumetinib, combined with SHP2 inhibitor, blocked RAS-MAPK overactivation, reduced fibrosis, and promoted bone union in Nf1-deficient tibial pseudarthrosis mouse model.
annotation_note: MEK1/2 has approved inhibitors (selumetinib) with direct pharmacology on RAS-pathway-driven Schwann-lineage tumor cells, relevant to essentially all NF1-driven tumors.

mechanism: MEK1/2 inhibitor mirdametinib suppresses ERK signaling, reducing HR gene transcription, synergizing with radiation to inhibit NF1-deficient glioblastoma growth in vitro/in vivo.
annotation_note: MEK1/2 has approved inhibitors (selumetinib) with direct pharmacology on RAS-pathway-driven Schwann-lineage tumor cells, relevant to essentially all NF1-driven tumors.

mechanism: Merlin loss activates hippo/YAP-TAZ-TEAD1 signaling in Schwann cells, driving proliferation, macrophage chemotaxis, and angiogenesis; TEAD1/YAP-TAZ inhibition (VT3989 and other TEADi) reversed tumorigenic signaling and reduced tumor cell survival in human VS cultures and NF2 mouse model.
annotation_note: TEAD has clinical-stage direct inhibitors (e.g. VT3989); acts on Schwann-lineage tumor cells downstream of germline Merlin/NF2 loss present in essentially all NF2-SWN patients.

mechanism: NF2 loss raises nuclear YAP/TAZ, driving TEAD-dependent CTGF and ALDH1A1 expression; YAP/TAZ knockdown or TEAD palmitoylation inhibitors block proliferation and shrink VG/DRG tumours in vivo and reduce human/mouse schwannoma proliferation.
annotation_note: TEAD palmitoylation inhibitors directly and druggably block YAP/TAZ-TEAD signaling in NF2-null Schwann-lineage tumor cells themselves, relevant across essentially all NF2-driven tumors.

mechanism: ABCC8 splice mutation (c.4412-2A>G) in NF-1 patient causes aberrant splicing/loss-of-function, identified as PAH-gene modifier of moyamoya syndrome via minigene assay.
mutation_context: ABCC8 splice mutation c.4412-2A>G, rare patient-specific modifier variant associated with moyamoya/pulmonary vasculopathy in NF1, frequency unknown/not population-wide
annotation_note: ABCC8 acts here as a vascular-modifier biomarker for pulmonary/moyamoya risk in a rare genotype, not a Schwann-cell drug target; K-ATP channel pharmacology (sulfonylureas) would act on vascular smooth muscle, a stromal compartment.

mechanism: CRISPR screen identifies ACSL3 as synthetic-lethal with NF2 loss; knockdown/knockout kills NF2-KO Schwann cells and reduces xenograft tumor growth via ferroptosis from lipid peroxidation.
annotation_note: ACSL3 is a druggable enzyme exploitable as synthetic-lethal ferroptosis induction in NF2-null schwannoma cells themselves, relevant to essentially all NF2-SWN tumors, not a distinct genotype subset.

mechanism: ADAM9 mRNA/protein overexpressed in VS tumor Schwann cells vs healthy nerve; secreted 68kDa isoform correlates with hearing impairment severity, proposed prognostic marker/therapeutic target.
annotation_note: ADAM9 is overexpressed in VS Schwann cells with a secreted isoform correlating with hearing loss, supporting prognostic biomarker use over direct drug targeting.

mechanism: RRM2 knockdown suppressed AKT-mTOR signaling; RRM2 overexpression activated AKT pathway to promote NF1-associated MPNST cell proliferation
annotation_note: AKT/mTOR is directly druggable (e.g. rapalogs, AKT inhibitors) in Schwann-lineage MPNST cells downstream of RRM2, relevant to all NF1-driven MPNST, not tumor microenvironment.

mechanism: NF1 loss hyperactivates AKT/mTOR signaling (via RAS-GAP suppression); pharmacologic AKT/mTOR inhibition (MK2206, rapamycin, Raptor KD) reduces Ccl5 expression in M-GBM cells.
annotation_note: AKT/mTOR is directly druggable (MK2206, rapamycin/analogs) and acts on the NF1-null glioma tumor cell itself, reducing Ccl5; germline NF1 loss affects essentially all patients.

mechanism: Neurofibromin-deficient ECs show enhanced Akt phosphorylation; PI3K-Akt inhibitor wortmannin blocks NF1KD-driven proliferation, network formation, and Nf1+/- aortic ring EC sprouting.
annotation_note: AKT is directly druggable (allosteric/ATP-competitive inhibitors exist) and mediates NF1-loss-driven proliferation in both tumor Schwann/glial cells and endothelium; germline NF1 loss affects essentially all patients.

mechanism: Akt hyperactivated in Nf1-deficient astrocytes/optic glioma; Akt inhibition reduces proliferation and tumor volume via Akt-dependent mTOR activation.
annotation_note: AKT is directly druggable (allosteric/ATP-competitive inhibitors exist) and mediates NF1-loss-driven proliferation in both tumor Schwann/glial cells and endothelium; germline NF1 loss affects essentially all patients.

mechanism: ALDH1A1 elevated in NF2-null human meningioma tissue and cell lines; shRNA knockdown of TAZ (not YAP) reduces ALDH1A1 protein, showing TAZ-dependent regulation in meningioma cells.
annotation_note: ALDH1A1 is a TAZ-driven tumor-cell-intrinsic marker of NF2-null Schwann/meningothelial cells; no approved or clinical-stage direct inhibitor exists, so it functions as a biomarker.

mechanism: ALDH1A1 upregulated in NF2-null mouse sciatic nerve/DRG and human schwannoma tissue; TAZ knockdown (not YAP loss) reduces ALDH1A1, confirming TAZ-dependent transcriptional regulation.
annotation_note: ALDH1A1 is a TAZ-driven tumor-cell-intrinsic marker of NF2-null Schwann/meningothelial cells; no approved or clinical-stage direct inhibitor exists, so it functions as a biomarker.

mechanism: AMPD3 elevated in NF1 fibroblasts/Schwann cells/plasma; siRNA knockdown reduces ERK signaling, proliferation, and induces apoptosis in NF1-associated Schwann cells, validating it as therapeutic target and biomarker.
annotation_note: AMPD3 knockdown affects ERK/proliferation/apoptosis in Schwann-lineage tumor cells and is elevated in NF1 tissue/plasma, making it useful as a biomarker despite early-stage siRNA-only evidence of direct pharmacology.

mechanism: AMPD3 elevated in NF1 fibroblasts/Schwann cells/plasma; siRNA knockdown reduces ERK signaling, proliferation, and induces apoptosis in NF1-associated Schwann cells, validating it as therapeutic target and biomarker.
annotation_note: AMPD3 knockdown affects ERK/proliferation/apoptosis in Schwann-lineage tumor cells and is elevated in NF1 tissue/plasma, making it useful as a biomarker despite early-stage siRNA-only evidence of direct pharmacology.

mechanism: ANXA3 upregulated in NF2-/- meningioma proteomics; knockdown reduced MCM2 and EdU proliferation in primary/grade3 cells and abolished tumour growth in NSG xenograft mouse model.
annotation_note: ANXA3 is upregulated in NF2-null meningioma tumour cells and drives proliferation; no established inhibitor exists, so it functions as a proliferation/prognostic marker and intrinsic tumour-cell target, not TME or mutation-subset restricted.

mechanism: Antioxidant apocynin reduced ROS production and macrophage infiltration, decreasing AngII-induced aortic aneurysm incidence/severity in Nf1+/- mice.
annotation_note: Apocynin is a direct NADPH-oxidase (NCF1/p47phox-CYBB) inhibitor acting on ROS-driven macrophage infiltration in vessel wall, a microenvironmental/vascular mechanism, not tumor-cell intrinsic.

mechanism: AR expression correlates with microvessel density, binds VEGFA promoter, promotes cell proliferation and angiogenesis; AR inhibitor MDV3100 suppresses these effects
annotation_note: AR acts in the tumour cell, where it binds the VEGFA promoter; the angiogenic effect on stroma is downstream of that, so the drug target is tumour-intrinsic.

mechanism: ATR inhibitors (AZD6738, VE-821) reduced survival in NF1-associated MPNST cell lines (NF90-8, ST88-14), enhanced in RECQL4-knockdown cells.
annotation_note: ATR is directly druggable (AZD6738, VE-821 are clinical-stage inhibitors) acting on the tumour cell itself, showing synthetic-lethal efficacy in NF1 glioma/MPNST lines.

mechanism: Serum AXL was significantly lower in NF1 patients with MPNST than those with high-load plexiform neurofibromas; AXL levels correlated with internal tumor burden, not significantly different from no-tumor patients.
annotation_note: Used here as a serum biomarker tracking tumor burden, not a drug target; AXL itself is druggable (e.g. bemcentinib) but acts mainly via TME/endothelial-immune signaling.

mechanism: HuR binds BRD2, BRD3, BRD4 mRNAs; HuR silencing reduces all three BET protein levels and genome-wide BRD2/3/4 chromatin occupancy (~45-60% loss), disrupting BRD-dependent transcriptional regulator networks in MPNST cells.
annotation_note: BET proteins are directly druggable by clinical-stage BET bromodomain inhibitors, acting on MPNST tumor cells themselves, not restricted to a NF1 subgenotype or the microenvironment.

mechanism: Schwannoma-derived HMGB1 induces neuronal CCL2 expression; CCL2 recruits CCR2+ macrophages into the DRG, which produce IL-6 causing pain.
annotation_note: CCL2 is a druggable chemokine (CCR2/CCL2 axis has clinical-stage antagonists) that acts on macrophage recruitment in the DRG microenvironment, not the tumor cell itself.

mechanism: CCL5 is autocrine growth/survival factor in NF1-mutant mesenchymal GBM; KD reduces cell survival in vitro and prolongs survival in vivo via CD44 to inhibit apoptosis.
annotation_note: CCL5 is a druggable chemokine (CCR5 antagonists exist) acting mainly via macrophage recruitment/autocrine signaling, so stromal/TME mechanism dominates despite some tumor-intrinsic autocrine role.

mechanism: YAP activation upregulates CCL5 secretion from cNF cells, promoting macrophage recruitment and proliferation, contributing to macrophage accumulation in cNF tumors.
annotation_note: CCL5 is a druggable chemokine (CCR5 antagonists exist) acting mainly via macrophage recruitment/autocrine signaling, so stromal/TME mechanism dominates despite some tumor-intrinsic autocrine role.

mechanism: CCR5 knockdown/overexpression in THP-1 macrophages altered p21/p27/PCNA and cell cycle, showing CCL5/CCR5 signaling drives macrophage proliferation in cNF microenvironment.
annotation_note: CCR5 has approved/clinical-stage antagonists (e.g. maraviroc) and here acts on macrophage proliferation in the cNF microenvironment, not the Schwann-cell tumor cell.

mechanism: Serum PD-L1 (CD274) significantly elevated in NF1 patients with MPNST versus those with plexiform neurofibroma or no tumor; authors propose it as biomarker and rationale for anti-PD-L1/PD-1 checkpoint immunotherapy.
annotation_note: Approved anti-PD-L1/PD-1 checkpoint agents exist, but here CD274 is used as a serum stratification biomarker and would act on tumor-infiltrating T cells/immune microenvironment, not the Schwann-lineage tumor cell.

mechanism: CD44 co-expressed with SPP1, NES, ERBB3 in SCP-like MPNST cells; CellChat shows CD44 as receiver of SPP1 signaling from macrophage cluster MAC-3, sustaining tumor stemness.
annotation_note: CD44 marks fibrotic/ECM-remodeled Schwann cells linked to bevacizumab resistance and macrophage-SCP crosstalk, favoring biomarker/stromal-signaling use over direct tumor-cell drug target.

mechanism: CD44 co-expressed with SPP1, NES, ERBB3 in SCP-like pNF cells; spatial transcriptomics shows CD44 co-localized with SPP1-expressing SCP-like/macrophage spots, supporting autocrine signaling loop.
annotation_note: CD44 marks fibrotic/ECM-remodeled Schwann cells linked to bevacizumab resistance and macrophage-SCP crosstalk, favoring biomarker/stromal-signaling use over direct tumor-cell drug target.

mechanism: CD44 acts as unconventional CCL5 receptor in M-GBM cells; KD increases apoptosis and abolishes Ccl5-induced growth stimulation.
annotation_note: CD44 marks fibrotic/ECM-remodeled Schwann cells linked to bevacizumab resistance and macrophage-SCP crosstalk, favoring biomarker/stromal-signaling use over direct tumor-cell drug target.

mechanism: CD74, the MIF receptor, is undetectable in normal nerve but strongly increased in mouse and human PN, expressed on Schwann cells, macrophages, and DCs; can activate NF-κB/RAS-MAPK.
annotation_note: CD74/MIF axis is druggable (anti-CD74 or MIF antagonists) but acts mainly via macrophages/DCs and stromal signaling in the PN microenvironment, not the Schwann-cell tumor clone itself.

mechanism: CDK4/6 are hyperactivated downstream of RABL6A via loss of p27 and cyclin D/CDK4/6 upregulation; CDK4/6 inhibitors (e.g., palbociclib) tested in MPNST models, with efficacy modulated by RABL6A levels.
annotation_note: CDK4/6 has approved clinical-stage inhibitors (e.g., palbociclib) acting directly on hyperproliferative Schwann-lineage MPNST tumor cells, not restricted to a genetic subgroup.

mechanism: CDKN2A/B loss occurs in NF1-associated premalignant neurofibroma/ANNUBP and is cited as a key acquired event driving malignant progression to MPNST, alongside PRC (SUZ12/EED) alterations.
mutation_context: CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion/loss in neurofibroma-to-MPNST progression; reported in ~simple majority of MPNSTs but not present in benign neurofibromas or germline NF1 alone
annotation_note: CDKN2A/B loss is a deletion event with no direct drug target, best used to flag malignant transformation risk and select CDK4/6-inhibitor therapy in tumor cells.

mechanism: CDKN2A/B loss occurs in NF1-associated premalignant neurofibroma/ANNUBP and is cited as a key acquired event driving malignant progression to MPNST, alongside PRC (SUZ12/EED) alterations.
mutation_context: CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion/loss in neurofibroma-to-MPNST progression; reported in ~simple majority of MPNSTs but not present in benign neurofibromas or germline NF1 alone
annotation_note: CDKN2A/B loss is a deletion event with no direct drug target, best used to flag malignant transformation risk and select CDK4/6-inhibitor therapy in tumor cells.

mechanism: NF2 mutants form IRF3-induced condensates sequestering PP2A/TBK1, suppressing cGAS-STING signaling; NF2m-IRF3 condensates observed in 7/11 human VS specimens.
annotation_note: STING agonists could reactivate suppressed cGAS-STING signaling directly in NF2-null schwannoma tumour cells; germline NF2 loss defines the disease, not a subset.

mechanism: DCAF1 overexpressed in Merlin-deficient meningioma tissue/cells vs normal; MLN3651-mediated CRL4-DCAF1 inhibition increased LATS1/2, reduced proliferation and viability, activated apoptosis in meningioma cells.
annotation_note: CRL4-DCAF1 is directly druggable (MLN3651 inhibits it, restoring LATS1/2 and killing Merlin-deficient meningioma cells), acting on the tumor cell itself in essentially all NF2-SWN patients.

mechanism: M-CSF correlated positively with CD68 and CD163 macrophage markers and with Ki-67/VEGF, supporting a role in macrophage infiltration linked to VS growth.
annotation_note: CSF1/CSF1R has clinical-stage inhibitors (e.g. pexidartinib) and would act on macrophages within the VS microenvironment, not the schwannoma cell itself.

mechanism: GM-CSF expression increased significantly with higher VS tumor volume and correlated positively with tumor volume in growth-rate subgroup analysis.
annotation_note: GM-CSF correlates with VS tumor volume, suggesting biomarker use; as a drug target it would act on tumor-associated macrophages/microenvironment, not schwannoma cells themselves.

mechanism: GM-CSFR-α is expressed on PNF myeloid cells (DCs, macrophages) and increased in PNF vs control, but genetic deletion of GM-CSFR-α did not reduce tumor number or myeloid infiltration.
annotation_note: GM-CSFR-α marks PNF-infiltrating myeloid cells (biomarker of macrophage/DC infiltration) but genetic deletion failed to reduce tumor burden, arguing against it as a TME drug target despite compartment fit.

mechanism: Genetic deletion of GM-CSFR-βc in Nf1 f/f;DhhCre mice reduced PNF tumor number and decreased tumor-associated Iba1+ macrophages and CD11c+ dendritic cells, independent of GM-CSF ligand.
annotation_note: CSF2RB (GM-CSFRβc) is druggable on tumor-associated macrophages/dendritic cells, acting on the PNF microenvironment rather than Schwann-lineage tumor cells; relevant to all NF1 PNF, not a mutation-restricted subset.

mechanism: Cxcl10 uniquely upregulated in neurofibroma-prone Nf1 mice, expressed by Schwann cell subsets; signals via Cxcr3 to recruit T cells/DCs driving neurofibroma initiation
annotation_note: CXCL10-CXCR3 signaling recruits immune cells (T cells/DCs) in the microenvironment; chemokine axis is a pharmacodynamic/initiation marker rather than a validated drug target itself.

mechanism: Global Cxcr3 deletion prevented neurofibroma formation in Nf1 mice; Cxcr3 expressed on T cells/DCs necessary for sustained macrophage infiltration and tumor development
annotation_note: CXCR3 antagonists exist and target immune cells (T cells/DCs/macrophages) in the tumor microenvironment, not the Nf1-null Schwann cell itself.

mechanism: Dcn expression increased specifically in PN Schwann cell subpopulations (MSC1, MSC2, NMSC, SGC) versus normal nerve, identified as a top upregulated gene by scRNA-seq in mouse PNs.
annotation_note: Decorin is a secreted ECM proteoglycan marking Schwann/stromal subpopulations; useful as expression biomarker, not a direct drug target.

mechanism: DLK1 overexpression reactivates embryonic/stem programs, drives immunosuppressive microenvironment, associates with worse survival; potential biomarker/therapeutic target in NF1-MPNST
annotation_note: DLK1 lacks credible direct inhibitors; overexpression on Schwann-lineage MPNST cells makes it chiefly a prognostic/biomarker candidate, though its immunosuppressive TME effects are secondary.

mechanism: EGFR/ErbB phosphorylation increased after anti-IL-6 treatment; EGFR TKI dacomitinib alone or combined with anti-IL-6 delayed schwannoma tumor growth in PDX models.
annotation_note: EGFR is druggable on the tumor cell itself (lapatinib clinically active in NF2 VS/meningioma); relevant broadly via NF2-loss-driven EGFR upregulation, not a specific subset mutation.

mechanism: Anti-IL-6 induced EGFR/ErbB2/3 phosphorylation as an escape mechanism; combined EGFR (dacomitinib) and IL-6 blockade controlled pain and tumor growth together.
annotation_note: EGFR is druggable on the tumor cell itself (lapatinib clinically active in NF2 VS/meningioma); relevant broadly via NF2-loss-driven EGFR upregulation, not a specific subset mutation.

mechanism: EGFR overexpressed in NF2-associated meningiomas; loss of NF2 upregulates EGFR; lapatinib (EGFR/ErbB2 inhibitor) shows growth-inhibitory effect on meningiomas clinically.
annotation_note: EGFR is druggable on the tumor cell itself (lapatinib clinically active in NF2 VS/meningioma); relevant broadly via NF2-loss-driven EGFR upregulation, not a specific subset mutation.

mechanism: EGFR expression/phosphorylation increased upon PTPRS knockdown, driving EMT and migration in NF1-deficient Schwann cells; correlates with recurrence and tumor size
annotation_note: EGFR is druggable on the tumor cell itself (lapatinib clinically active in NF2 VS/meningioma); relevant broadly via NF2-loss-driven EGFR upregulation, not a specific subset mutation.

mechanism: HuR is elevated in human MPNST tissue and cell lines; genetic and pharmacological HuR inhibition blocks tumor formation, induces regression of established xenografts, and suppresses lung metastatic colonization.
annotation_note: HuR is overexpressed (not mutated) in MPNST tumor cells themselves; genetic/pharmacological inhibition is directly antitumor, a real druggable mechanism relevant across NF1-MPNST.

mechanism: EPHA2 receptor phosphorylation (pEPHA2) is activated in NF2-null Schwann cells and human VS tumors independent of mTORC1/2; dasatinib inhibits pEPHA2 and downstream pAkt, contributing to tumor growth inhibition.
annotation_note: EPHA2 is druggable (dasatinib inhibits pEPHA2/pAkt) and acts directly on NF2-null Schwann tumor cells, not the microenvironment; relevant to all NF2-driven VS.

mechanism: pEPHB1 identified as top activated kinase in NF2-null meningioma cells via kinome screen; inhibited by dasatinib as part of therapeutic strategy
annotation_note: pEPHB1 is a druggable activated kinase in NF2-null meningioma cells, targetable by dasatinib directly on the tumour cell, relevant to all NF2-loss meningiomas.

mechanism: ErbB2 overexpressed in meningiomas; regulation of ErbB2 affects meningioma cell proliferation/apoptosis/invasion in vitro; lapatinib targets ErbB2 with clinical growth-inhibitory effect.
annotation_note: ErbB2 is overexpressed/activated in NF2-related meningioma and vestibular schwannoma tumour cells and is directly druggable by lapatinib, a clinical-stage inhibitor.

mechanism: ErbB2 overexpressed/phosphorylated in VS tissue and heregulin-stimulated cells; lapatinib inhibited ErbB2 activation, proliferation, and survivin upregulation.
annotation_note: ErbB2 is overexpressed/activated in NF2-related meningioma and vestibular schwannoma tumour cells and is directly druggable by lapatinib, a clinical-stage inhibitor.

mechanism: Brigatinib potently inhibits FAK1(PTK2) by kinome profiling and reduces p-FAK in Ben-Men-1 meningioma cells and xenograft tumors, correlating with tumor shrinkage.
annotation_note: FAK1/PTK2 is directly druggable (brigatinib inhibits p-FAK) in NF2-null Schwann/meningioma tumor cells themselves, relevant to all NF2 patients, not a stromal target.

mechanism: Brigatinib inhibits FAK1(PTK2) in Schwann/schwannoma cells and Postn-Cre;Nf2 flox/flox mouse DRG/schwannoma tissue, reducing p-FAK and tumor/DRG volume.
annotation_note: FAK1/PTK2 is directly druggable (brigatinib inhibits p-FAK) in NF2-null Schwann/meningioma tumor cells themselves, relevant to all NF2 patients, not a stromal target.

mechanism: Kinome profiling shows brigatinib strongly and reproducibly inhibits FER in NF2-deficient meningioma (Syn5, Ben-Men-1) cells; validated by NanoBRET assay.
annotation_note: FER is a druggable kinase directly inhibited by brigatinib in NF2-deficient schwannoma and meningioma tumor cells, not merely a biomarker.

mechanism: FGF1 and FGF2 transcripts upregulated largely in MSC2 Schwann cells in PNs; CellPhoneDB predicts these ligands act on receptors expressed by stromal cell populations in mouse/human PN.
annotation_note: FGF1/2 are druggable secreted ligands (FGFR inhibitors exist) acting paracrine from MSC2 Schwann cells onto stromal/receptor-bearing microenvironment populations in PN, not a tumor-intrinsic mutation-defined marker.

mechanism: Merlin loss upregulates FOXM1; FOXM1 knockdown reduces ICG-001 sensitivity, showing FOXM1 mediates Wnt/β-catenin-driven meningioma growth inhibition.
annotation_note: FOXM1 is a druggable transcription factor (e.g. thiostrepton) acting in Merlin-deficient meningioma tumor cells via Wnt/β-catenin signaling, relevant to essentially all NF2-SWN meningiomas.

mechanism: G6PD inhibition selectively kills NF2-KO Schwann cells and shrinks xenograft tumors; synthetic lethality rescued by NAC, reflecting reliance on G6PD-derived NADPH for redox balance.
annotation_note: G6PD is a druggable metabolic enzyme; synthetic lethality exploits NF2-null Schwann cell redox dependence, acting directly on tumor cells, not a subset mutation or stroma.

mechanism: Schwann cell-derived GDNF activates neuronal GFRα1 on HTMRs and C-fibers; AAV shRNA knockdown of GFRα1 reduced mechanical hypersensitivity and afferent sensitization in NF1 mice.
annotation_note: GFRα1 is a neuronal receptor druggable by knockdown/antagonism to block GDNF-driven pain signaling; not a tumor-cell or biomarker target, relevant to all NF1 patients.

mechanism: GHS-R immunohistochemically detected in all cutaneous neurofibromas; percentage/intensity of positive cells correlates with tumor volume and female gender, suggesting ghrelin-GHSR axis role in tumorigenesis.
annotation_note: GHSR is a GPCR with ghrelin-axis ligands (e.g., ghrelin mimetics/antagonists) but here it's evidenced only as an IHC correlate of tumor volume, favoring biomarker use on Schwann-lineage tumor cells.

mechanism: Fimepinostat targets HDAC2 specifically, inducing p21 upregulation, cell cycle arrest, and caspase-3/7-dependent apoptosis in NCH1 spinal (non-vestibular) schwannoma cells.
annotation_note: Fimepinostat is a clinical-stage HDAC (HDAC2) inhibitor acting directly on schwannoma tumor cells, relevant to NF2-SWN broadly, not TME or a specific subtype.

mechanism: Fimepinostat targets HDAC2, driving p21 upregulation, cell cycle arrest, and caspase-3/7 apoptosis in patient VS cells and model lines, with in vivo tumor regression in allografts.
annotation_note: Fimepinostat is a clinical-stage HDAC (HDAC2) inhibitor acting directly on schwannoma tumor cells, relevant to NF2-SWN broadly, not TME or a specific subtype.

mechanism: HIF-1α positive in 75.6% of MPNST specimens and independently predicted poor survival; siRNA knockdown suppressed MPNST cell proliferation and induced apoptosis/subG1 increase under hypoxia; chetomin inhibited HIF-1α transcriptional activity, blocked growth, induced apoptosis.
annotation_note: HIF-1α drives MPNST tumor cell survival under hypoxia and is directly druggable (chetomin/siRNA), acting on tumor cells, not stroma, across NF1 patients generally.

mechanism: Schwannoma-secreted HMGB1 upregulates neuronal CCL2 expression, driving macrophage recruitment to the DRG and pain; HMGB1 knockdown reduced macrophage infiltration and pain.
annotation_note: HMGB1 is a druggable secreted alarmin; mechanism acts via neuronal CCL2 and macrophage recruitment to DRG, a microenvironment/immune pain pathway, not tumor-cell-intrinsic.

mechanism: H-Ras(G12V) binds Gal-1 via specific residues; Gal-1 chaperones activated Ras at plasma membrane, driving Ras/Erk oncogenic signaling in MPNST; disrupted by LLS30.
mutation_context: HRAS G12V activating mutation; rare in NF1 MPNST, not present in most patients
annotation_note: G12V-mutant HRAS drives tumor-cell Ras/Erk signaling via Gal-1; disruptable, restricted to HRAS-mutant MPNST subset.

mechanism: BIRC5 (survivin, an IAP) amplified in human MPNST; survivin highly expressed in MPNST cell lines; knockdown/inhibition abrogated growth and reduced metastases in xenografts.
annotation_note: IAP inhibitors (e.g. Smac mimetics targeting survivin/XIAP) are clinical-stage direct pharmacology acting on the MPNST tumor cell itself, relevant broadly, not a defined genotype subset.

mechanism: DRG macrophages overproduce IL-6 (highest induced cytokine) after tumor stimulation; anti-IL-6 antibody treatment reduced pain in PDX models but had modest tumor effect.
annotation_note: IL-6 has approved inhibitors (tocilizumab/siltuximab) and acts on DRG macrophages/pain signaling, a microenvironment/neuroimmune mechanism, not the Schwann-lineage tumor cell itself.

mechanism: Activated IRF3 binds mutant NF2 FERM domain, inducing condensates that block TBK1 activation; NF2m-IRF3 condensates found in VS patient specimens.
annotation_note: IRF3 is druggable via disrupting NF2m-IRF3 condensates/restoring TBK1 signaling in schwannoma cells, relevant to all NF2-null VS, not immune/stromal.

mechanism: Combined cordycepin/FT895 treatment suppressed KIF18A protein via reduced TEAD1 promoter binding, causing microtubule/chromosome mis-segregation and aneuploidy in MPNST cells.
annotation_note: KIF18A is a mitotic kinesin druggable in tumor cells themselves; emerging KIF18A inhibitors exist, and here it drives MPNST cell aneuploidy, not TME or genotype-restricted biology.

mechanism: c-KIT among top kinases activated upon NF2 loss in meningioma cells; dasatinib, a c-KIT inhibitor, blocks activation as therapeutic approach
annotation_note: Imatinib is a credible direct KIT inhibitor, but the NF1 mechanism is SCF/c-kit+ mast cell recruitment, i.e. microenvironment-driven tumorigenesis.

mechanism: Nf1-deficient Schwann cells secrete SCF recruiting c-kit+ mast cells; hematopoietic c-kit ablation and imatinib (c-kit inhibitor) block/reduce tumorigenesis
annotation_note: Imatinib is a credible direct KIT inhibitor, but the NF1 mechanism is SCF/c-kit+ mast cell recruitment, i.e. microenvironment-driven tumorigenesis.

mechanism: Nf1-null Schwann cells secrete high levels of stem cell factor (KITLG), recruiting and activating Nf1+/- c-kit-expressing mast cells that drive tumor growth
annotation_note: KITLG/c-kit signaling is druggable (e.g., imatinib) and acts on tumor-associated mast cells in the microenvironment, not the Nf1-null Schwann cell itself.

mechanism: KSR1 significantly overexpressed in Merlin-deficient meningioma tissue and primary cells versus normal meninges/HMC; correlates with DCAF1 expression, implicating role in tumourigenic signalling.
annotation_note: KSR1 is a scaffold protein lacking direct inhibitors; overexpression marks Merlin-deficient meningioma tumour cells, not stroma.

mechanism: KYNU marks a metabolically active SPP1+KYNU+ macrophage subset with upregulated tryptophan metabolism; IDO1 inhibition reversed macrophage-induced tumor cell migration and cytokine secretion, and this subset correlated with Treg/exhausted T cell infiltration.
annotation_note: KYNU marks a macrophage subset driving tryptophan/IDO1-linked immunosuppression; better used as a biomarker of this TME state than as a direct drug target itself.

mechanism: KYNU marks a metabolically active SPP1+KYNU+ macrophage subset with upregulated tryptophan metabolism; IDO1 inhibition reversed macrophage-induced tumor cell migration and cytokine secretion, and this subset correlated with Treg/exhausted T cell infiltration.
annotation_note: KYNU marks a macrophage subset driving tryptophan/IDO1-linked immunosuppression; better used as a biomarker of this TME state than as a direct drug target itself.

mechanism: LGALS1-encoded Gal-1 acts as Ras chaperone stabilizing active Ras at membrane; elevated in MPNST; LLS30 targets Gal-1/Ras pocket, suppressing Ras/Erk, tumor growth and metastasis.
annotation_note: Gal-1 directly chaperones Ras at the tumor cell membrane; LLS30 inhibits this pocket, acting on Schwann-lineage MPNST cells, not stroma.

mechanism: Selumetinib combined with MLN3651 blocked MLN3651-induced pERK1/2 increase and had additive effect reducing proliferation/viability in Merlin-deficient meningioma cells; DCAF1 knockdown reduced KSR1 association with pMEK1/2/pERK1/2 in HEK293T cells.
annotation_note: MEK1/2 has approved inhibitors (selumetinib) with direct pharmacology on RAS-pathway-driven Schwann-lineage tumor cells, relevant to essentially all NF1-driven tumors.

mechanism: In an NF2 patient, selumetinib monotherapy for 3 months produced a partial response in a thoracic intramedullary tumor consistent with ependymoma, quantified by reduced contrast enhancement.
annotation_note: MEK1/2 has approved inhibitors (selumetinib) with direct pharmacology on RAS-pathway-driven Schwann-lineage tumor cells, relevant to essentially all NF1-driven tumors.

mechanism: NF1-mutant JMML is RAS-dependent; MEKi (mirdametinib, selumetinib, trametinib) improved survival, blood counts, and spleen size in Kras/Nras/Nf1-driven mouse JMML models
annotation_note: MEK1/2 has approved inhibitors (selumetinib) with direct pharmacology on RAS-pathway-driven Schwann-lineage tumor cells, relevant to essentially all NF1-driven tumors.

mechanism: This paper studies trametinib (MEK inhibitor) treatment of progressive pLGG driven by MAPK pathway alterations (BRAF-fusion, NF1, FGFR1), showing disease control via MAPK inhibition.
annotation_note: MEK/RAF inhibitors (e.g., trametinib, selumetinib) directly and effectively target MAPK pathway activation driven by germline NF1 loss in essentially all NF1 patients, acting on the tumor cell itself.

mechanism: NF1 loss elevates Ras-GTP activating Raf/MEK/Erk-MAPK proliferation; Krox20-cre and Nf1-/-:Nf1+/+ mouse models producing plexiform neurofibromas support this cascade.
annotation_note: MEK/RAF inhibitors (e.g., trametinib, selumetinib) directly and effectively target MAPK pathway activation driven by germline NF1 loss in essentially all NF1 patients, acting on the tumor cell itself.

mechanism: ERK1/2 strongly phosphorylated in all VS tissue samples and confirmed by IHC; heregulin-induced ERK1/2 activation blocked by lapatinib in schwannoma cells.
annotation_note: ERK1/2 is a druggable downstream RAS-MAPK effector active in essentially all NF1/NF2-driven tumours, acting directly on Schwann-lineage tumour cells; MEK/ERK inhibitors are clinical-stage.

mechanism: ME1 mRNA/protein/activity are reduced in NF2-KO Schwann cells and patient vestibular schwannomas; ME1 and G6PD redundantly supply NADPH, and combined loss causes lethality.
annotation_note: ME1 loss is a metabolic vulnerability marker in NF2-null Schwann tumor cells reflecting synthetic lethality with G6PD, not a direct drug target with credible inhibitors.

mechanism: MET is a cabozantinib target kinase identified by MIB/MS with decreased binding after treatment, implicated in tumor response in Nf1 mutant PN mouse model.
annotation_note: MET is a directly druggable RTK (cabozantinib target) active on Schwann-lineage plexiform neurofibroma cells, relevant broadly in Nf1-driven PN rather than a specific subset genotype.

mechanism: SCP-like cells uniquely express MIF in mouse and human PN; CellPhoneDB predicts MIF signals through CD74 on macrophages/DCs, and MIF/CD74 signaling can activate NF-κB and MAPK.
annotation_note: MIF is druggable (clinical-stage MIF/CD74 inhibitors exist), but mechanism is SCP-to-macrophage signaling, acting on the microenvironment rather than tumor cells.

mechanism: MMP9 is secreted by schwannoma cells, upregulated via TNF-α, drives invasion, adhesion molecule expression (N-cadherin, αvβ3), and its inhibition reduces tumor growth in vivo.
annotation_note: MMP9 is a secreted protease driven by schwannoma cells themselves (TNF-α induced) with credible small-molecule/antibody inhibitors, so it acts on the tumor cell/ECM invasion axis, not primarily stroma.

mechanism: MRVI1 p.P186S variant confirmed in a European NF-1 patient with moyamoya syndrome, consistent with prior report of co-segregation as MMS modifier.
mutation_context: MRVI1 p.P186S variant, reported in single NF1 patients with moyamoya syndrome; frequency not established, not present in most NF1 patients
annotation_note: MRVI1 P186S is a rare candidate modifier variant linked to moyamoya vasculopathy risk stratification in NF1, not a druggable tumour-cell target.

mechanism: MTAP protein loss detected by IHC in 5/5 ANNUBP samples, linked to CDKN2A co-deletion during NF1-associated progression from neurofibroma toward MPNST.
mutation_context: MTAP/CDKN2A co-deletion, ~85% of MPNSTs; not present in benign neurofibromas
annotation_note: MTAP loss marks malignant transformation; deletion itself undruggable, though it creates PRMT5-inhibitor synthetic-lethal vulnerability.

mechanism: MTAP is co-deleted with CDKN2A during NF1-associated neurofibroma-to-MPNST progression; IHC shows MTAP loss in 85% of MPNSTs and correlates with malignant transformation and high-grade disease.
mutation_context: MTAP/CDKN2A co-deletion, ~85% of MPNSTs; not present in benign neurofibromas
annotation_note: MTAP loss marks malignant transformation; deletion itself undruggable, though it creates PRMT5-inhibitor synthetic-lethal vulnerability.

mechanism: Everolimus (mTOR inhibitor) plus selumetinib was given to this ependymoma-harboring patient but discontinued after 2 weeks due to grade III mucositis and rash before efficacy assessment.
annotation_note: mTOR is directly druggable (everolimus, AZD2014) acting on the tumor cell itself in NF1/NF2-driven tumors, relevant across essentially all patients with these manifestations.

mechanism: NF-κB pathway activated in PN Schwann cells and immune cells; nuclear p65 elevated in Nf1-mutant SCs, human PN tissue, and SCP-like colonies; IκB dominant-negative reduced Nf1-null sphere formation.
annotation_note: NF-κB inhibitors (e.g. IKK/proteasome-based) directly target pathway activation in Nf1-null Schwann cell lineage cells, relevant to essentially all PN, not immune/stromal compartment.

mechanism: PRC2 loss activates Notch pathway genes/proteins (NOTCH1/3, JAG1, HES1) in iHSCs and MPNST lines; gamma-secretase inhibitor nirogacestat inhibits Notch processing and synergizes with MEK inhibitor in MPNST cells.
annotation_note: Nirogacestat is a clinical-stage gamma-secretase inhibitor directly blocking Notch processing in MPNST tumour cells, relevant broadly via PRC2 loss rather than a specific subset mutation.

mechanism: Tissue immunofluorescence showed ANNUBP tumors had the highest nuclear ODC activity (>10 nmol/min/ug) of all tumor types studied, suggesting lower likelihood of benefit from DFMO/ODC inhibition than lower-ODC tumors.
annotation_note: DFMO is a credible clinical-stage direct ODC1 inhibitor acting on tumor Schwann-lineage cells, though ODC activity also serves as a stratification biomarker.

mechanism: Nuclear ODC activity, measured by quantitative immunofluorescence on a tissue microarray, was low to moderate (<5 nmol/min/ug) in most MPNST samples, proposed as favorable for DFMO responsiveness.
annotation_note: DFMO is a credible clinical-stage direct ODC1 inhibitor acting on tumor Schwann-lineage cells, though ODC activity also serves as a stratification biomarker.

mechanism: Grade 1 neurofibroma (NF) samples showed ODC activity mostly below 5 nmol/min/ug via tissue immunofluorescence, though one NF sample exceeded 10 nmol/min/ug, indicating heterogeneity within this tumor type.
annotation_note: DFMO is a credible clinical-stage direct ODC1 inhibitor acting on tumor Schwann-lineage cells, though ODC activity also serves as a stratification biomarker.

mechanism: Olaparib (PARP1 inhibitor) combined with Selumetinib significantly suppressed tumor growth (61.6% reduction) in NF1-18B MPNST PDOX mouse model; PARylation loss confirmed target engagement.
annotation_note: PARP1 is directly druggable (olaparib) acting on tumor Schwann-cell lineage via synthetic lethality with MEK inhibition, relevant broadly to NF1-MPNST, not a specific subclone genotype.

mechanism: PDLIM2 identified by proteomics as upregulated in Merlin-deficient primary meningioma cells and Ben-Men-1 vs meningeal cells; validated by Western blot; shRNA knockdown significantly reduced Ki-67+ proliferation in primary meningioma cells.
annotation_note: PDLIM2 is a Merlin-deficiency-driven proliferation dependency in tumor cells themselves (schwannoma/meningioma), with knockdown data supporting it as a direct pharmacological target, not merely a marker.

mechanism: PDLIM2 identified by proteomics/phospho-proteomics as upregulated in Merlin-deficient primary schwannoma vs Schwann cells; validated by Western blot; shRNA knockdown significantly reduced Ki-67+ proliferation in primary schwannoma cells.
annotation_note: PDLIM2 is a Merlin-deficiency-driven proliferation dependency in tumor cells themselves (schwannoma/meningioma), with knockdown data supporting it as a direct pharmacological target, not merely a marker.

mechanism: Merlin loss triggers TβR1-mediated phosphorylation/degradation of RKIP; RKIP-stabilizing agents Nf18001 and PRG-N-01 inhibit tumor growth, promote Schwann cell differentiation, and shrink vestibular nerve tumors in preclinical/trial models.
annotation_note: RKIP itself is drugged directly by TβR1-blocking small molecules (PRG-N-01) that restore RKIP in NF2-deficient Schwann cells, relevant to all Merlin-null schwannomas.

mechanism: PRG-N-01 binds TβR1 kinase domain (230-322), blocking TβR1-RKIP interaction and preventing RKIP phosphorylation/degradation, restoring RKIP levels and suppressing NF2-deficient schwannoma growth in vivo and in vitro.
annotation_note: RKIP itself is drugged directly by TβR1-blocking small molecules (PRG-N-01) that restore RKIP in NF2-deficient Schwann cells, relevant to all Merlin-null schwannomas.

mechanism: PI3K/Akt hyperactivated downstream of Nf1 loss; PI3K inhibition decreases Nf1 optic glioma volume, proliferation, and retinal ganglion cell loss.
annotation_note: PI3K inhibitors (e.g., pictilisib) directly target hyperactivated PI3K in tumour Schwann/glioma cells downstream of NF1/NF2 loss, present in essentially all patients.

mechanism: PLK1 was top hit in drug and siRNA screens of NF1 MPNST cells (ST88-14); PLK1 inhibitor BI6727 stabilized tumor volume in MPNST xenografts, causing G2 arrest and multinucleation.
annotation_note: PLK1 is directly druggable (clinical-stage inhibitor BI6727) and acts on the Schwann-lineage MPNST tumor cell itself, causing mitotic arrest, not the microenvironment.

mechanism: Postn is the top marker gene of the de novo SCP-like Schwann cell population in mouse PNs, also elevated in NMSCs, and described as a sustained injury-response gene.
annotation_note: POSTN is a marker of an SCP-like/injury-response Schwann cell state and matrix-associated stroma, useful for tumor classification rather than direct drug targeting.

mechanism: PP2A A (PPP2R1A/B) and C (PPP2CA) subunit expression and phosphatase activity are reduced in human/mouse neurofibroma tissue and Schwann cells; FTY720 restores PP2A activity, inhibits sphere formation/proliferation, induces apoptosis, and reduces tumor number in mice.
annotation_note: PP2A activity is pharmacologically restorable (e.g. FTY720) directly in Schwann-lineage tumor cells, relevant to essentially all NF1/NF2 neurofibromas, not immune/stromal.

mechanism: PRMT5 expression and activity (H4R3me2s) were elevated in all 5 ANNUBP samples with MTAP loss, indicating compensatory PRMT5 dependency in this NF1-associated premalignant stage.
mutation_context: MTAP deletion/loss (co-deleted with CDKN2A) in MPNST and ANNUBP, seen in subset of NF1 tumors, exact NF1-population frequency not well established
annotation_note: PRMT5 inhibitors act directly on MTAP-deficient Schwann-lineage tumor cells via synthetic lethality, not stroma; restricted to MTAP-deleted subset.

mechanism: PRMT5 is upregulated with MTAP loss in NF1-associated and sporadic MPNST; genetic/chemical PRMT5 inhibition selectively impaired MTAP-deficient MPNST cell growth via DNA damage and G2/M arrest, synergizing with chemotherapy.
mutation_context: MTAP deletion/loss (co-deleted with CDKN2A) in MPNST and ANNUBP, seen in subset of NF1 tumors, exact NF1-population frequency not well established
annotation_note: PRMT5 inhibitors act directly on MTAP-deficient Schwann-lineage tumor cells via synthetic lethality, not stroma; restricted to MTAP-deleted subset.

mechanism: PROS1 is expressed by stromal, immune, and some Schwann cells; CellPhoneDB predicts PROS1 signals via AXL to SCP-like cells, other SC types, and stromal/immune cells in PN.
annotation_note: PROS1-AXL is a secreted-ligand/receptor axis signaling from stromal/immune cells to Schwann-lineage cells; AXL inhibitors exist, so mechanism is microenvironmental, not tumor-cell-intrinsic.

mechanism: PTEN, a tumor suppressor regulating PI3K/AKT/TOR, is significantly downregulated in MPNST vs neurofibroma and proposed as a biomarker for TOR-inhibitor efficacy.
annotation_note: PTEN loss is a tumor-suppressor deletion/downregulation acting on Schwann-lineage tumor cells, useful as a stratification biomarker for TOR-inhibitor response, not itself druggable.

mechanism: SHP2 inhibition (SHP099) lowers RAS-GTP, blocks RAF/MEK/ERK signaling, suppresses MPNST cell growth and tumor volume, extends survival in allograft and PDX models; combination with hydroxychloroquine prevents/delays resistance.
annotation_note: SHP2 has a credible clinical-stage direct inhibitor (SHP099) acting on RAS-MAPK in NF1-null Schwann/MPNST tumor cells, relevant to essentially all NF1 patients, not tumor microenvironment.

mechanism: SHP2 (PTPN11) inhibitor SHP099, combined with MEK inhibitor, reduced RAS-MAPK signaling upstream of RAS, restored chondrogenic fate, and prevented tibial pseudarthrosis in Nf1-deficient mice.
annotation_note: SHP2 has a credible clinical-stage direct inhibitor (SHP099) acting on RAS-MAPK in NF1-null Schwann/MPNST tumor cells, relevant to essentially all NF1 patients, not tumor microenvironment.

mechanism: PTPRS downregulated in PNF tissue, suppresses EMT/migration by inhibiting EGFR expression/phosphorylation; low PTPRS correlates with recurrence
annotation_note: PTPRS is a downregulated tumour-suppressor phosphatase in Schwann-lineage PNF cells; no direct activator exists, so its value is as a prognostic/recurrence biomarker, not a drug target.

mechanism: RABL6A is an oncogenic GTPase essential for MPNST progression, inactivating RB1 by hyperactivating CDKs (via p27 loss) and activating MEK/Myc, sensitizing cells to CDK4/6 inhibitors.
annotation_note: RABL6A is an oncogenic GTPase acting cell-intrinsically in Schwann-lineage tumor cells; loss sensitizes to CDK4/6 inhibitors, a real pharmacological handle, not just a marker.

mechanism: MEKi decreases RAD51 transcription/foci in NF1-deficient glioblastoma, creating HR-deficient state that sensitizes tumors to radiation-induced DNA damage.
annotation_note: RAD51 is directly druggable (e.g., RI-1) to block HR repair in tumor Schwann/glioma cells, sensitizing them to radiation; relevant broadly, not TME.

mechanism: RAD51-mediated homologous recombination repairs radiation-induced DNA double-strand breaks in VS cells; RAD51 inhibitor RI-1 blocks repair, enhancing radiation-induced cell death.
annotation_note: RAD51 is directly druggable (e.g., RI-1) to block HR repair in tumor Schwann/glioma cells, sensitizing them to radiation; relevant broadly, not TME.

mutation_context: MN1 overexpression/amplification reported in a subset of NF1-associated MPNSTs; exact population frequency not established
annotation_note: MN1 is a nuclear transcriptional coregulator with no ligand-binding pocket or clinical inhibitor, better suited as a prognostic/stratification marker in MPNST subsets.

Clemastine promotes oligodendrocyte precursor differentiation/remyelination, a repurposed antimuscarinic with credible direct pharmacology on the glial lineage, not tumor stroma or a genotype-restricted subset.

mechanism: PAK1/2 directly bind Merlin; PAK inhibition (FRAX-1036, G-5555, NVS-PAK1-1) reduces proliferation in NF2-deficient schwannoma cell lines, synergizing with TEAD inhibition.
annotation_note: PAK1/2 have clinical-stage inhibitors (FRAX-1036, G-5555, NVS-PAK1-1) acting directly on NF2-null schwannoma tumour cells, relevant to essentially all NF2 patients, not a stromal target.

SCF/KIT signaling drives mast cell recruitment in plexiform neurofibroma stroma; imatinib targets this KIT axis therapeutically.
SCN9A (Nav1.7) is a validated direct drug target for pain signaling in sensory neurons, relevant to NF1 pain broadly, not tumor microenvironment or a mutation subset.
SERPINB4 is a serpin overexpressed in MPNST tissue, useful as a diagnostic/classification marker of tumor cells; no established direct inhibitor exists.

mechanism: pSrc/SFK (Y416) phosphorylation is elevated in primary human VS tumors and mouse allograft tumors and reduced by dasatinib treatment, independent of mTORC1/2 signaling.
annotation_note: SFKs are directly druggable (dasatinib) in Schwann-cell-lineage VS tumor cells, relevant to essentially all NF2 patients, not a specific tumor microenvironment mechanism.

mechanism: SGK1 (mTORC2 target) is constitutively activated with NF2 loss in meningioma, cited from prior work; this paper's own new data on SGK1 activation is in NF2-null Schwann cells/VS, not meningioma.
annotation_note: SGK1 is an mTORC2-driven kinase druggable by SGK1 inhibitors, acting in NF2-null tumour cells themselves, not restricted to a patient subgroup or the microenvironment.

mutation_context: PRC2-deficient (SUZ12/EED-loss) NF1-mutant MPNST subgroup, a minority of MPNSTs
annotation_note: SHH/SMO is druggable (vismodegib/sonidegib precedent) and acts on the Schwann-lineage tumor cell, but activation is restricted to PRC2-deficient NF1 MPNST subgroup.

mechanism: SOX10 silencing via chromatin closure occurs in 3KO NC model representing early MPNST-like stage; ANNUBP samples show high SOX10 expression in glial component, not silencing.
annotation_note: SOX10 is a lineage/cell-of-origin and chromatin-state marker (loss marks MPNST progression) rather than a directly druggable transcription factor target.

mechanism: SPRED1/2 loss phenocopies NF1 loss; both cooperate to regulate RAS-independent MAPK-AKT signaling and downstream EMT-associated gene signatures (CDH11, COL1A1, IGFBP2, SEMA3C) in MEF and NF1 patient Schwann/nerve cells.
annotation_note: SPRED1/2 are tumour suppressors whose loss (not an inhibitable protein) phenocopies NF1 loss in Schwann-lineage cells; loss status is more useful as a classifier/marker than a drug target.
TBK1 is a druggable kinase with clinical-stage inhibitors; acts directly on NF2-null schwannoma cells (e.g. via Hippo/YAP survival signaling), not restricted to a subgenotype or the microenvironment.

TEAD1 is a druggable Hippo-pathway transcription factor (TEAD/YAP-TAZ inhibitors in clinical development) acting directly on MPNST/schwannoma tumor cells, relevant across NF1/NF2 patients, not a specific subclone marker.
